$description: EDH Seer MOVES ALMOST NOTHING. The client defines exactly one animation - a panel revealing on entry - plus the force simulation the graph runs, which is physics rather than choreography. The five-duration, five-easing, six-keyframe library that used to sit here described no shipped motion.

reveal.$description: the one animation's own duration. Above the 300ms UI-transition ceiling because it is an entrance for a whole panel, not a state change on a control.

ease-out.$description: the only curve the product uses - entrances decelerate

reveal-up.$description: `@keyframes reveal-up` / `.reveal`. Opacity 0 to 1 with a 6px rise: enough to read as arriving, small enough that a page of panels does not lurch.

reducedMotion.$description: `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { .reveal { animation: none } }` - the animation is removed outright, not shortened. It carries no information, so there is nothing to preserve as a fade.
